description: An operator can define and iterate on project purposes without writing code
naive_change: `residual add purpose` CLI command
outcomes: operator adds purposes tied to an attractor without writing code

description: An operator can retrieve all current project context before starting a skill session
naive_change: `residual skill-data <name>` prints formatted markdown context
outcomes: operator begins skill sessions with current residual context

description: An operator can install skills into any supported agent's config directory without manual file management
naive_change: `residual skill-install --agent <name>` command
outcomes: operator installs skill files without manual file copying

description: Data integrity is enforced before any commit touches residual/ files
naive_change: pre-commit git hook runs `residual verify all`
outcomes: operator cannot commit invalid traits or broken attractor links

description: The NKP matrix provides visual evidence of hyperliminal coupling and fusion/fission candidates
naive_change: `residual matrix show` with colored table output
outcomes: operator surfaces hyperliminal coupling without manual matrix calculation

description: Skills self-report their version so an operator can detect and respond to staleness
naive_change: Version field in skill front-matter; `residual skill-check` command
outcomes: operator detects when a cached skill is outdated

description: The LLM interface accepts metadata additions in any order, at any phase, without explicit skill invocation or context switching — an operator records architecture as it comes to them
naive_change: Conversational metadata entry: stressors, purposes, terms, and attractors can be added mid-session without phase discipline or skill ceremony
outcomes: operator records stressor narratives without switching between skill phases

description: An operator can start and complete residuality workflow artifacts without outside input; consulting others remains desirable but optional
naive_change: residual init + skill-data/skill sessions + verify all; core residual/ structure required
outcomes: operator produces a residual tree that passes verify without outside input

description: An operator follows residuality a-la-carte — required core residual structure, optional skill sequence — so existing operator workflows remain feasible
naive_change: skills and CLI treat purpose-walk through ATAM as selectable steps; verify enforces structure not ceremony
outcomes: operator completes residual work using only the skill steps their workflow needs

description: An operator surfaces stressors from multiple personas so lone or small-team walks are not limited to a single perspective; default adequacy is two personas — one stakeholder and one direct user — unless the operator sets a different bar
naive_change: residual/personas/*.md consumed by stressor-walk; default walk expects stakeholder + direct-user personas; later outcome: empirically derive alpha/beta perspective-heterogeneity coefficients and encode them
outcomes: operator records stressors drawn from at least two personas including one stakeholder and one direct user; outcome includes eventual empirical alpha/beta encoding for perspective heterogeneity

description: An operator explores application state space fully as stressors explored and attractors discovered
naive_change: stressors.csv + attractors.csv as the primary exploration ledger; schema omits probability fields because probability-framing narrows attention to pre-weighted futures and blocks discovery of unforeseen attractors
outcomes: operator records stressors and attractors that constitute the explored state space

description: An operator records residues that answer stressors by changing hardware, process, organization, or policy when that zig survives better than a software-only zag
naive_change: naive_change (and later residues) accept whole-system-residue; skills and CLI prompt for non-software zig before software patch
outcomes: operator records whole-system-residue when the surviving change leaves the software boundary

description: An operator judges residual-architecture quality by progress toward criticality and by comparing naive-architecture versus residual-architecture survival across recorded stressors (Ri), not by pattern compliance
naive_change: residual matrix criticality + residual matrix ri
outcomes: operator computes criticality and Ri from residual artifacts after stressor exposure

description: Residual-architecture demonstrates longitudinal superiority in real environments by surviving more foreseen and unforeseen stressors past an Ri threshold
naive_change: design and execute a controlled longitudinal study comparing residuality-guided architectures against risk/pattern baselines; publish protocol and results
outcomes: outcome evidences residual-architecture survival past the Ri threshold across recorded stressors

description: Operators and prospects can see robustness of the method through studies and through encoded perspective-heterogeneity (alpha/beta), so efficacy is communicable not merely asserted
naive_change: published study artifacts plus documented alpha/beta derivation path tied to persona-driven walks
outcomes: operator communicates residual-architecture robustness to a prospect via study outcomes and persona measures

description: Every attractor carries both positive and negative state pressure so operators know what/why/how keeps the attractor going and what failure looks like
naive_change: attractor records expose positive_state and negative_state (replacing single valence classification); skills require both sides before an attractor is considered defined
outcomes: operator defines each attractor with a positive state and a negative state

description: Purposes and stressors express outcomes — including modes of operation and ways of being — with schema and CLI language aligned to outcome rather than one-off feature checklists alone
naive_change: rename/extend purpose feature+traits fields toward outcome semantics in CLI and CSV while preserving verify
outcomes: operator records outcomes that encode end states or modes of operation using defined terminology

description: Git history uses project lexicon and component vocabulary so operators can read architectural intent from git log
naive_change: commit-msg hook + verify commit-msg validate subject against lexicon/components/forces
outcomes: operator reads commit history using defined outcome

description: Architectural insights from personas are maximized when each persona runs as an isolated subagent with staged analysis rather than inline alongside the main conversation
naive_change: Persona walks in later phases use isolated subagents that go through staged analysis: initial skepticisms and desires, attractor review, full force review, then handled/unhandled analysis before reporting to the parent
outcomes: personas generate forces and residues reflecting the real state space; each persona produces a handled/unhandled analysis that surfaces genuinely unaddressed concerns

description: An agent or operator invoking any skill on an uninitialized project is guided by skill data to establish the three primitives in the correct order and form before analysis begins
naive_change: skill data emits a Bootstrap Required section with attractor, stressor, and purpose definitions and bootstrapping steps when the ledger is uninitialized or underspecified
outcomes: operator establishes attractor, stressor, and purpose primitives before beginning skill analysis

description: An operator reviews force descriptions against the architecture iteration's ergodic boundary after capture.
naive_change: An operator-invoked post-capture heuristic scans force descriptions for component lexicon terms and presents matches without storing classifications or blocking verification.
outcomes: Operator revises a flagged force that primarily describes a component dynamic. Operator leaves a flagged force unchanged when its source exists primarily beyond the ergodic boundary.

description: An operator can consult ordered environmental evidence without treating it as a complete account of the hyperliminal.
naive_change: Only when prompted, the agent asks which material under residual/research/ the operator wants reviewed and how it should inform the session. The agent challenges restrictive or context-polluting use; tooling neither loads research automatically nor prescribes its organization.
outcomes: Operator chooses research context for a requested review. Agent challenges research use that excludes coherent forces or pollutes the working context.

description: An operator periodically reopens the recorded stressor and attractor landscape as real-world configurations change.
naive_change: A non-blocking pre-commit hook compares last purpose-walk and stressor-walk completion against an operator-defined interval; .walk-review.toml on the git-sidecar branch holds state; prompts operator to revisit stressors and attractors when elapsed.
outcomes: Operator maintains criticality by routinely taking architecture walks. Operator revises and extends forces and attractors as new evidence builds.

description: An agent records the first mechanistic adjustment proposed in response to each stressor or purpose.
naive_change: Skill guidance and CLI help define naive_change through paired force, mechanism, and outcome examples.
outcomes: Agent describes what changes in the system under naive_change. Agent describes the desired end state under outcome.

description: An actor records outcomes as states the residual-architecture should preserve under force.
naive_change: Skill and CLI prompts separately request environmental pressure, mechanistic adjustment, desired outcome, and unchecked attractor state.
outcomes: Actor records the desired outcome under a stressor. Actor links the stressor to an attractor whose negative state describes unchecked pressure.

description: An agent communicates ledger concepts in terms an operator can follow without side-channel lookup.
naive_change: Skills render attractor names and force shortnames in dialogue, adding IDs only on first reference or where a command requires them.
outcomes: Agent and operator maintain shared comprehension of the active forces and attractors across a walk.

description: Organizations carry real institutional trust in the methodology investments they already have — TDD, DDD, Clean or Onion architecture, or others. An operator who treats residuality as a wholesale replacement for that investment, rather than something that sits alongside and strengthens it, forfeits the credibility that comes from respecting existing practice.
naive_change: Generalize both fixed-ideology skills — naive-draft's hardcoded vertical-slices/APOSD drafting method and tdd-implement's hardcoded R/G-TDD loop — into pluggable methodology slots that sit alongside the org's existing practice rather than replacing it.
outcomes: operator's residual-architecture output complements the org's existing methodology rather than replacing it

description: Different organizations, teams, and even different projects within the same organization favor different architecture-drafting and implementation ideologies, and that preference changes over time. A tool that hardcodes one drafting methodology and one implementation loop cannot follow an operator across organizational or project boundaries without forcing a mismatch between the ledger's methodology assumptions and the ideology actually in use.
naive_change: Two pluggable methodology-skill slots — drafting and implementation — replacing the two currently hardcoded skills.
outcomes: operator swaps drafting and implementation methodology skills while the same skill continues to consume the ledger

description: Non-practitioners evaluate architectural claims through whatever mental model they already hold, and that model is often locked — fixed enough that vocabulary mismatch alone, not the reasoning's quality, causes the claim to be dismissed. An operator needs to theorize in advance how a given outsider will receive residuality-derived reasoning, and catalog which framings land and which trigger rejection — distinct from the reasoning itself.
naive_change: A separate ledger, parallel to the core five files — not a single skill, not a naive_change bolted onto an existing stressor — dedicated to theorizing and cataloging interactions with outsiders: which audiences hold which locked priors, which translated framings have landed or failed historically, which channels are safe for raw vs. translated artifacts.
outcomes: operator communicates residual-architecture insight to a non-practitioner using a vetted framing

description: An operator can add a component to the registry without hand-editing components.csv
naive_change: residual add component --name <name> --description <desc> --status <proposed|actual> --architecture-set <set>, mirroring the ID-generation and idempotency guards the other add subcommands already have
outcomes: operator adds a component using the CLI

description: An operator can remove or repoint a residue coupling without hand-editing residues.csv
naive_change: residual remove residue --force-id <ID> --component-id <ID> (or a --move-to <component> flag on add residue), guarded by the same verify/session-hash checks that already protect other mutating commands - the destructive-agent risk the omission was originally hedging against
outcomes: operator repoints residue coupling using the CLI

description: An operator can keep residual metadata synchronized to the specific working branch it describes, edit that metadata locally beside the config file, and have every working-branch commit mirrored into the matching git-sidecar branch automatically.
naive_change: Add residual branch edit/save/merge subcommands plus an operator-defined branch-name pattern setting, and a post-commit hook that mirrors each working-branch commit into the matching git-sidecar branch — without blocking residual/config.toml itself from committing normally on the working branch.
outcomes: operator materializes git-sidecar metadata beside the config file for editing | residues stay synchronized with the branch that produced them | git-sidecar commits carry the working branch's commit title and hash

description: An agent preserves the residual ledger across compaction by carrying forward decisions, dead ends, corrections, and already-completed additions rather than ceremony.
naive_change: Have skill-hooks provide a compact pre-compaction ledger prompt and a post-compaction reminder to consult skills-guru for the next relevant step.
outcomes: The compacted agent retains usable residual context and checks skills-guru before deciding what to do next.

description: An agent receives occasional guru guidance selected from the discussion rather than a generic reminder every fixed number of turns.
naive_change: Let skill-hooks classify the active discussion against guru topics, apply per-topic cadence and deduplication, and emit only an applicable suggestion.
outcomes: Guru prompts appear when the active work warrants them and do not become background noise.
